sanskrit: yaś ca diṣṭaparo loke yaś cāyaṃ haṭhavādakaḥ ubhāv apasadāv etau karmabuddhiḥ praśasyate
english: He who in the world is wholly given to fate, and he who insists only on willful exertion — both of these are base; the intelligence that abides in action is to be praised.

sanskrit: yo hi diṣṭam upāsīno nirviceṣṭaḥ sukhaṃ svapet avasīdet sudurbuddhir āmo ghaṭa ivāmbhasi
english: For he who, relying on fate, sleeps in ease without any effort, sinks down in utter foolishness like an unbaked pot in water.

sanskrit: tathaiva haṭhabuddhir yaḥ śaktaḥ karmaṇy akarmakṛt āsīta na ciraṃ jīved anātha iva durbalaḥ
english: Likewise he who is governed by willfulness, though capable of action, sits doing nothing — he would not live long, like a weak man without a protector.

sanskrit: akasmād api yaḥ kaś cid arthaṃ prāpnoti pūruṣaḥ taṃ haṭheneti manyante sa hi yatno na kasya cit
english: When any man whatsoever attains a result without apparent cause, they attribute it to willful effort; yet that effort truly belongs to no one in particular.

sanskrit: yac cāpi kiṃ cit puruṣo diṣṭaṃ nāma labhaty uta daivena vidhinā pārtha tad daivam iti niścitam
english: And whatever a man obtains that is called fate, O Pārtha, which comes by divine ordinance — that is certainly declared to be destiny.

sanskrit: yat svayaṃ karmaṇā kiṃ cit phalam āpnoti pūruṣaḥ pratyakṣaṃ cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ tat pauruṣam iti smṛtam
english: Whatever fruit a man attains by his own action, directly seen with the eye — that is remembered as human effort.

sanskrit: svabhāvataḥ pravṛtto 'nyaḥ prāpnoty arthān akāraṇāt tat svabhāvātmakaṃ viddhi phalaṃ puruṣasattama
english: Another, acting by natural disposition, obtains results without apparent cause — know that fruit to be the product of inherent nature, O best of men.

sanskrit: evaṃ haṭhāc ca daivāc ca svabhāvāt karmaṇas tathā yāni prāpnoti puruṣas tat phalaṃ pūrvakarmaṇaḥ
english: Thus what a man obtains through willful effort, fate, natural disposition, and action — all that fruit is the result of deeds done in a former life.

sanskrit: dhātāpi hi svakarmaiva tais tair hetubhir īśvaraḥ vidadhāti vibhajyeha phalaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ nṛṇām
english: For the Creator himself, as the lord, through those very causes, ordains and distributes here below the fruit of former deeds for men.

sanskrit: yad dhy ayaṃ puruṣaḥ kiṃ cit kurute vai śubhāśubham tad dhātṛvihitaṃ viddhi pūrvakarmaphalodayam
english: Whatever good or evil this man does — know that to be ordained by the Creator, the arising of the fruit of former karma.

sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ tasya deho 'yaṃ dhātuḥ karmaṇi karmaṇi sa yathā prerayaty enaṃ tathāyaṃ kurute 'vaśaḥ
english: This body is the instrument for his deeds in each action; as the Creator impels it, so this man acts helplessly.

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu hi kṛtyeṣu viniyoktā maheśvaraḥ sarvabhūtāni kaunteya kārayaty avaśāny api
english: In each and every task the Great Lord is the director; all beings, O son of Kuntī, he causes to act even against their will.

sanskrit: manasārthān viniścitya paścāt prāpnoti karmaṇā buddhipūrvaṃ svayaṃ dhīraḥ puruṣas tatra kāraṇam
english: Having resolved upon goals in the mind, a wise man thereafter attains them through action guided by his intellect — he himself is the cause therein.

sanskrit: saṃkhyātuṃ naiva śakyāni karmāṇi puruṣarṣabha agāranagarāṇāṃ hi siddhiḥ puruṣahaitukī
english: The deeds of men cannot even be enumerated, O bull among men; the success of households and cities is indeed caused by human effort.

sanskrit: tile tailaṃ gavi kṣīraṃ kāṣṭhe pāvakam antataḥ dhiyā dhīro vijānīyād upāyaṃ cāsya siddhaye
english: As oil lies in the sesame seed, milk in the cow, fire latent in the wood — a wise man should discern these through intelligence, and also the means for their extraction.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravartate paścāt karaṇeṣv asya siddhaye tāṃ siddhim upajīvanti karmaṇām iha jantavaḥ
english: Thereafter he proceeds to the means for its accomplishment; creatures here below subsist on that success born of their actions.

sanskrit: kuśalena kṛtaṃ karma kartrā sādhu viniścitam idaṃ tv akuśaleneti viśeṣād upalabhyate
english: Work done by a skilled person is determined by the doer to be well done; that done by the unskilled is known to be deficient — one perceives this clearly through the distinction.

sanskrit: iṣṭāpūrtaphalaṃ na syān na śiṣyo na gurur bhavet puruṣaḥ karmasādhyeṣu syāc ced ayam akāraṇam
english: There would be no fruit of sacred rites and charitable works, no pupil, no teacher — if this man were without agency in matters accomplished by action.

sanskrit: kartṛtvād eva puruṣaḥ karmasiddhau praśasyate asiddhau nindyate cāpi karmanāśaḥ kathaṃ tv iha
english: Solely because of agency is a man praised when his action succeeds; likewise he is blamed when it fails — how then can action be destroyed here?

sanskrit: sarvam eva haṭhenaike diṣṭenaike vadanty uta puruṣaprayatnajaṃ ke cit traidham etan nirucyate
english: Some say everything arises from willful effort alone; others say from fate alone; some say from human endeavor — this is declared as threefold.

sanskrit: na caivaitāvatā kāryaṃ manyanta iti cāpare asti sarvam adṛśyaṃ tu diṣṭaṃ caiva tathā haṭhaḥ dṛśyate hi haṭhāc caiva diṣṭāc cārthasya saṃtatiḥ
english: Others again hold that one should not act on this basis alone — everything unseen exists, and so do fate and willful effort; for from both willful effort and fate is seen the continuity of results.

sanskrit: kiṃ cid daivād dhaṭhāt kiṃ cit kiṃ cid eva svakarmataḥ puruṣaḥ phalam āpnoti caturthaṃ nātra kāraṇam kuśalāḥ pratijānanti ye tattvaviduṣo janāḥ
english: Something from fate, something from willful effort, something from one's own action — a man obtains his fruit; there is no fourth cause, so declare the wise who know the truth.

sanskrit: tathaiva dhātā bhūtānām iṣṭāniṣṭaphalapradaḥ yadi na syān na bhūtānāṃ kṛpaṇo nāma kaś cana
english: Likewise the Creator who bestows desired and undesired fruits upon beings — if he did not exist, there would be no one wretched among beings.

sanskrit: yaṃ yam artham abhiprepsuḥ kurute karma pūruṣaḥ tat tat saphalam eva syād yadi na syāt purākṛtam
english: Whatever purpose a man desires and acts to achieve — that would bear fruit in every case, if there were no prior deeds.

sanskrit: tridvārām arthasiddhiṃ tu nānupaśyanti ye narāḥ tathaivānarthasiddhiṃ ca yathā lokās tathaiva te
english: Those men who do not perceive success in results through these three doors, and likewise the arising of failure — they are as the common people are.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ tv eva karmeti manor eṣa viniścayaḥ ekāntena hy anīho 'yaṃ parābhavati pūruṣaḥ
english: "Action indeed must be done" — this is Manu's firm conclusion; for one who is wholly indifferent to effort is completely overwhelmed.

sanskrit: kurvato hi bhavaty eva prāyeṇeha yudhiṣṭhira ekāntaphalasiddhiṃ tu na vindaty alasaḥ kva cit
english: For the one who acts here generally finds success, O Yudhiṣṭhira; but a lazy man never anywhere attains unqualified achievement of results.

sanskrit: asaṃbhave tv asya hetuḥ prāyaścittaṃ tu lakṣyate kṛte karmaṇi rājendra tathānṛṇyam avāpyate
english: When something proves impossible, the means of expiation is still to be observed; and when one has done what can be done, O king of kings, freedom from debt is thereby attained.

sanskrit: alakṣmīr āviśaty enaṃ śayānam alasaṃ naram niḥsaṃśayaṃ phalaṃ labdhvā dakṣo bhūtim upāśnute
english: Ill-fortune enters that man who lies sleeping in idleness; the capable man, obtaining results without doubt, enjoys prosperity.

sanskrit: anarthaṃ saṃśayāvasthaṃ vṛṇvate muktasaṃśayāḥ dhīrā narāḥ karmaratā na tu niḥsaṃśayaṃ kva cit
english: Wise men devoted to action, freed from doubt, choose the uncertain adverse outcome over the certain one; they never rest anywhere in absolute certainty.

sanskrit: ekāntena hy anartho 'yaṃ vartate 'smāsu sāṃpratam na tu niḥsaṃśayaṃ na syāt tvayi karmaṇy avasthite
english: For a definite misfortune prevails over us at this moment; yet if you were steadfastly engaged in action, there is no certainty it would remain so.

sanskrit: atha vā siddhir eva syān mahimā tu tathaiva te vṛkodarasya bībhatsor bhrātroś ca yamayor api
english: Or perhaps success itself would come, and great glory to you as well as to Vṛkodara, to Bībhatsu, and to the twin brothers.

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ karma saphalam asmākam api vā punaḥ viprakarṣeṇa budhyeta kṛtakarmā yathā phalam
english: The actions of others bear fruit; so too might ours again — one who has done the work understands in time what fruit it yields.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ lāṅgalenaiva bhittvā bījaṃ vapaty uta āste 'tha karṣakas tūṣṇīṃ parjanyas tatra kāraṇam
english: The farmer splits the earth with his plough alone and sows his seed, then sits silent — the rain-cloud is the cause therein.

sanskrit: vṛṣṭiś cen nānugṛhṇīyād anenās tatra karṣakaḥ yad anyaḥ puruṣaḥ kuryāt kṛtaṃ tat sakalaṃ mayā
english: If the rain should not favor this farmer, yet some other man acts — he may say, "All that was done has been done by me."

sanskrit: tac ced aphalam asmākaṃ nāparādho 'sti naḥ kva cit iti dhīro 'nvavekṣyaiva nātmānaṃ tatra garhayet
english: "If that proves fruitless for us, there is no fault in us anywhere" — having reflected thus, the wise man should not blame himself in that matter.

sanskrit: kurvato nārthasiddhir me bhavatīti ha bhārata nirvedo nātra gantavyo dvāv etau hy asya karmaṇaḥ siddhir vāpy atha vāsiddhir apravṛttir ato 'nyathā
english: "Though I act, no achievement of purpose comes to me" — O Bhārata, despondency must not be indulged on this account; for action has only these two outcomes: either success or failure; inaction is otherwise.

sanskrit: bahūnāṃ samavāye hi bhāvānāṃ karma sidhyati guṇābhāve phalaṃ nyūnaṃ bhavaty aphalam eva vā anārambhe tu na phalaṃ na guṇo dṛśyate 'cyuta
english: For it is through the convergence of many factors that action succeeds; when a quality is absent the fruit is deficient or entirely absent; yet in non-commencement no fruit and no merit are seen at all, O Acyuta.

sanskrit: deśakālāv upāyāṃś ca maṅgalaṃ svasti vṛddhaye yunakti medhayā dhīro yathāśakti yathābalam
english: A wise man employs place, time, means, and auspicious observances for prosperity through his intelligence, according to his capacity and his strength.

sanskrit: apramattena tat kāryam upadeṣṭā parākramaḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ karmayogeṣu sarva eva parākramaḥ
english: That must be done with diligence; an instructor of valor — in the application of action, all is indeed valor.

sanskrit: yaṃ tu dhīro 'nvavekṣeta śreyāṃsaṃ bahubhir guṇaiḥ sāmnaivārthaṃ tato lipset karma cāsmai prayojayet
english: Whoever a wise man, reflecting well, regards as superior in many virtues — by conciliation alone let him seek his aim from that one, and apply his action accordingly.

sanskrit: vyasanaṃ vāsya kāṅkṣeta vināśaṃ vā yudhiṣṭhira api sindhor girer vāpi kiṃ punar martyadharmiṇaḥ
english: Or let him await that one's misfortune or destruction, O Yudhiṣṭhira — even an ocean or a mountain meets its end; what then of one subject to mortal law?

sanskrit: utthānayuktaḥ satataṃ pareṣām antaraiṣaṇe ānṛṇyam āpnoti naraḥ parasyātmana eva ca
english: A man who is constantly devoted to effort, while looking for the openings of others, attains freedom from debt both toward others and toward himself.

sanskrit: na caivātmāvamantavyaḥ puruṣeṇa kadā cana na hy ātmaparibhūtasya bhūtir bhavati bhārata
english: Nor should a man ever despise himself; for one who has held himself in contempt will not find prosperity, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsthitikā siddhir iyaṃ lokasya bhārata citrā siddhigatiḥ proktā kālāvasthāvibhāgataḥ
english: Thus is success in the world constituted, O Bhārata; the varied movement of success has been described according to the divisions of time and circumstance.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ me pitā pūrvaṃ vāsayām āsa paṇḍitam so 'smā artham imaṃ prāha pitre me bharatarṣabha
english: My father formerly lodged a learned brahmin with him; that brahmin spoke this very teaching to my father, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: nītiṃ bṛhaspatiproktāṃ bhrātṝn me 'grāhayat purā teṣāṃ sāṃkathyam aśrauṣam aham etat tadā gṛhe
english: He formerly had my brothers learn the statecraft taught by Bṛhaspati; I heard their discourse on this very topic at home at that time.

sanskrit: sa māṃ rājan karmavatīm āgatām āha sāntvayan śuśrūṣamāṇām āsīnāṃ pitur aṅke yudhiṣṭhira
english: He spoke to me consolingly, O king, as I came eager for activity and sat in my father's lap attending respectfully, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yājñasenyā vacaḥ śrutvā bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ niḥśvasann upasaṃgamya kruddho rājānam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Yājñasenī, Bhīmasena, exceedingly impatient, sighing deeply, approached and spoke angrily to the king.

sanskrit: rājyasya padavīṃ dharmyāṃ vraja satpuruṣocitām dharmakāmārthahīnānāṃ kiṃ no vastuṃ tapovane
english: "Go forth on the righteous path of kingship, befitting good men — what is the use for us, bereft of dharma, pleasure, and wealth, in dwelling in the forest of austerity?

sanskrit: naiva dharmeṇa tad rājyaṃ nārjavena na caujasā akṣakūṭam adhiṣṭhāya hṛtaṃ duryodhanena naḥ
english: That kingdom was not taken from us by dharma, nor by honesty, nor by might; it was taken by Duryodhana resorting to the fraud of the dice.

sanskrit: gomāyuneva siṃhānāṃ durbalena balīyasām āmiṣaṃ vighasāśena tadvad rājyaṃ hi no hṛtam
english: As a jackal takes the prey of lions, as the weak takes the food of the strong, as a glutton seizes leftovers — so our kingdom has indeed been stolen.

sanskrit: dharmaleśapraticchannaḥ prabhavaṃ dharmakāmayoḥ artham utsṛjya kiṃ rājan durgeṣu paritapyase
english: Concealed by a pretense of dharma, having abandoned wealth — the source of dharma and pleasure — why, O king, do you torment yourself in these hardships?

sanskrit: bhavato 'nuvidhānena rājyaṃ naḥ paśyatāṃ hṛtam ahāryam api śakreṇa guptaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Through compliance with your command, as we watched helplessly, our kingdom was stolen — though it was protected by the Gāṇḍīva-bowman and could not have been taken even by Indra.

sanskrit: kuṇīnām iva bilvāni paṅgūnām iva dhenavaḥ hṛtam aiśvaryam asmākaṃ jīvatāṃ bhavataḥ kṛte
english: Like bilva fruits taken from the crippled, like cows taken from the lame — our sovereignty has been stolen while we live, because of you.

sanskrit: bhavataḥ priyam ity evaṃ mahad vyasanam īdṛśam dharmakāme pratītasya pratipannāḥ sma bhārata
english: Saying 'this is your wish' — we have accepted such a great calamity as this, O Bhārata, you who are devoted to dharma and pleasure.

sanskrit: karśayāmaḥ svamitrāṇi nandayāmaś ca śātravān ātmānaṃ bhavataḥ śāstre niyamya bharatarṣabha
english: We are causing our own allies to wither and giving joy to our enemies, restraining ourselves under your command, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yad vayaṃ na tadaivaitān dhārtarāṣṭrān nihanmahi bhavataḥ śāstram ādāya tan nas tapati duṣkṛtam
english: That we did not at that very moment slay these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having taken up your command — that evil deed torments us.

sanskrit: athainām anvavekṣasva mṛgacaryām ivātmanaḥ avīrācaritāṃ rājan na balasthair niṣevitām
english: Now look upon this life of wandering in the forest as your own — O king, this way of living unworthy of heroes, not pursued by those who stand in strength.

sanskrit: yāṃ na kṛṣṇo na bībhatsur nābhimanyur na sṛñjayaḥ na cāham abhinandāmi na ca mādrīsutāv ubhau
english: This way of life neither Kṛṣṇa nor Bībhatsu nor Abhimanyu nor Sṛñjaya approves — nor do I, nor do the two sons of Mādrī.

sanskrit: bhavān dharmo dharma iti satataṃ vratakarśitaḥ kaccid rājan na nirvedād āpannaḥ klībajīvikām
english: You are ever worn thin by vows, saying 'dharma, dharma' — have you, O king, through despondency fallen into the life of a eunuch?

sanskrit: durmanuṣyā hi nirvedam aphalaṃ sarvaghātinam aśaktāḥ śriyam āhartum ātmanaḥ kurvate priyam
english: Base men, unable to bring prosperity for themselves, resort to despondency — fruitless and destructive of everything — for their own pleasure.

sanskrit: sa bhavān dṛṣṭimāñ śaktaḥ paśyann ātmani pauruṣam ānṛśaṃsyaparo rājan nānartham avabudhyase
english: Yet you are far-sighted and capable, perceiving manliness in yourself — yet being devoted to non-cruelty, O king, you do not recognize what is harmful.

sanskrit: asmān amī dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ kṣamamāṇān alaṃ sataḥ aśaktān eva manyante tadduḥkhaṃ nāhave vadhaḥ
english: These sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra consider us, though enduring and truly virtuous, to be simply incapable — that is the sorrow; death in battle would not be.

sanskrit: tatra ced yudhyamānānām ajihmam anivartinām sarvaśo hi vadhaḥ śreyān pretya lokāṃl labhemahi
english: If, fighting there without crookedness and without retreat, total death would be better — we would gain the worlds hereafter.

sanskrit: atha vā vayam evaitān nihatya bharatarṣabha ādadīmahi gāṃ sarvāṃ tathāpi śreya eva naḥ
english: Or else, slaying them ourselves, O bull of the Bhāratas, we would take back the entire earth — even so that is indeed the better course for us.

sanskrit: sarvathā kāryam etan naḥ svadharmam anutiṣṭhatām kāṅkṣatāṃ vipulāṃ kīrtiṃ vairaṃ praticikīrṣatām
english: In every way this is what we must do — we who follow our own dharma, who desire vast glory, who wish to repay our enmity.

sanskrit: ātmārthaṃ yudhyamānānāṃ vidite kṛtyalakṣaṃṇe anyair apahṛte rājye praśaṃsaiva na garhaṇā
english: For those fighting in their own cause, when the nature of their duty is known and the kingdom has been seized by others — praise alone is fitting, not blame.

sanskrit: karśanārtho hi yo dharmo mitrāṇām ātmanas tathā vyasanaṃ nāma tad rājan na sa dharmaḥ kudharma tat
english: That dharma whose purpose is the wasting of friends and of oneself — that, O king, is called calamity, not dharma; that is false dharma.

sanskrit: sarvathā dharmanityaṃ tu puruṣaṃ dharmadurbalam jahatas tāta dharmārthau pretaṃ duḥkhasukhe yathā
english: A man perpetually devoted to dharma who yet abandons dharma when weakened by it — dharma and wealth leave him entirely, like a dead man's joys and sorrows.

sanskrit: yasya dharmo hi dharmārthaṃ kleśabhāṅ na sa paṇḍitaḥ na sa dharmasya vedārthaṃ sūryasyāndhaḥ prabhām iva
english: He whose dharma bears nothing but suffering in the cause of dharma — he is no wise man; he does not know the meaning of dharma, as a blind man knows not the radiance of the sun.

sanskrit: yasya cārthārtham evārthaḥ sa ca nārthasya kovidaḥ rakṣate bhṛtako 'raṇyaṃ yathā syāt tādṛg eva saḥ
english: He for whom wealth exists solely for wealth's own sake — he too is not wise about wealth; he is like a hired man guarding a forest: the forest is his in name only.

sanskrit: ativelaṃ hi yo 'rthārthī netarāv anutiṣṭhati sa vadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmaheva jugupsitaḥ
english: He who pursues wealth beyond measure and does not practice the other two — he is fit to be slain by all beings and is despised like a killer of a brahmin.

sanskrit: satataṃ yaś ca kāmārthī netarāv anutiṣṭhati mitrāṇi tasya naśyanti dharmārthābhyāṃ ca hīyate
english: He who is always in pursuit of pleasure and does not practice the other two — his friends perish and he falls away from both dharma and wealth.

sanskrit: tasya dharmārthahīnasya kāmānte nidhanaṃ dhruvam kāmato ramamāṇasya mīnasyevāmbhasaḥ kṣaye
english: For him who is bereft of dharma and wealth, destruction at the end of pleasure is certain — like a fish delighting in water when the water runs dry.

sanskrit: tasmād dharmārthayor nityaṃ na pramādyanti paṇḍitāḥ prakṛtiḥ sā hi kāmasya pāvakasyāraṇir yathā
english: Therefore the wise are never negligent in the constant pursuit of dharma and wealth; for the nature of pleasure is like the fire-drill of fire — the fire of desire springs from dharma and wealth.

sanskrit: sarvathā dharmamūlo 'rtho dharmaś cārthaparigrahaḥ itaretarayonī tau viddhi meghodadhī yathā
english: Wealth is in every way rooted in dharma, and dharma in its turn depends on the support of wealth — know these two as each other's source, like the cloud and the ocean.

sanskrit: dravyārthasparśasaṃyoge yā prītir upajāyate sa kāmaś cittasaṃkalpaḥ śarīraṃ nāsya vidyate
english: The delight that arises from the conjunction of the object of material sense with the senses — that is desire, a mental resolve; it has no body of its own.

sanskrit: arthārthī puruṣo rājan bṛhantaṃ dharmam ṛcchati artham ṛcchati kāmārthī na kāmād anyam ṛcchatī
english: The man who seeks wealth, O king, attains great dharma; the man who seeks pleasure attains wealth as well; but from pleasure alone nothing other than pleasure is obtained.

sanskrit: na hi kāmena kāmo 'nyaḥ sādhyate phalam eva tat upayogāt phalasyeva kāṣṭhād bhasmeva paṇḍitaḥ
english: For desire does not accomplish any further desire — that is its only fruit; as from consuming a fruit one gets only ash from the wood — so says the wise man.
